clue.text: I look up one article on another fairy tale

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first article sits above the second
in a down clue, up means the word for look is written climbing the column, so backwards

parts.note: lo is an old word for look, as in lo and behold
an is an indefinite article
the is another article, the definite one

explanation.surface: A reader peers up from one item to another and finds a fairy story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns LO into OL. IOLANTHE is the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera whose heroine is a fairy.
explanation.definitionFit: Iolanthe is an operetta about a fairy who married a mortal, so it is literally a fairy's tale.

clue.text: Time to joke, entering into extra financial burden?

indicators.note: entering into says the time-and-joke pair goes inside the word for extra

parts.note: more means extra, additional
a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A wry question whether there is time for a joke while a debt grows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering into' puts TGAG inside MORE.
explanation.definitionFit: A home loan is the classic financial burden most households carry for decades.

clue.text: A little poem for Proust's girl?

definitions.text: A little poem for Proust's girl?

parts.words: A little poem for Proust's girl?
parts.note: a short ode, with the diminutive ending -ette run into it, gives the name of the courtesan Swann loves in Proust

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a short verse would suit a character from Proust.
explanation.walkthrough: ODE plus the diminutive suffix -ETTE, sharing the E, makes 'a little poem'. Odette de Crécy is Swann's beloved in Proust's In Search of Lost Time.
explanation.definitionFit: Odette is the woman Swann obsesses over in Proust's novel, so she is the novelist's girl.

clue.text: Noble rank open to knight: earl

indicators.note: open to says the word for rank is split apart to admit the knight

parts.note: a grade is a rank or level
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: An aristocratic order of precedence that admits a knight and an earl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open to' puts N inside GRADE.
explanation.definitionFit: A grandee is a high-ranking Spanish or Portuguese aristocrat, hence any nobleman of standing.

clue.text: Strangely, a peer and me touring Hungary may fly together

indicators.note: touring says the shuffled letters travel round the abbreviation for Hungary
strangely says the letters of peer and me come out in an odd order

parts.note: H is the international vehicle code for Hungary

explanation.surface: A lord and the speaker travel oddly around Hungary together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges PEERME and 'touring' puts that round H, with A added at the end. Ephemera is the genus name of mayflies, so the definition reads as 'mayfly' split into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Ephemera is the scientific name for a genus of mayflies, so a collection of them is mayflies together.

clue.text: One lawyer in casual dress beneath consideration

indicators.note: in says the one and the lawyer go inside the word for casual dress

parts.note: a negligé, the French spelling of negligee, is a light, loose dressing gown
I is the Roman numeral for one
BL is a Bachelor of Law

explanation.surface: A lawyer turns up in casual wear, which is beneath anyone's notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts IBL inside NEGLIGEE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something negligible is so small or unimportant that it can safely be ignored.

clue.text: Looks for audience: they fit in well

indicators.note: for audience says the word for looks is to be heard, not read

parts.note: stares are long looks

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a crowd's attention and fits in well with others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they fit in well' means a stairwell, the shaft a staircase is built in, not people fitting in socially.
explanation.definitionFit: A staircase is built inside a stairwell, the vertical shaft in a building.

clue.text: Mrs Jellyby, for one, should improve, speaking ungrammatically

definitions.meaning: Mrs Jellyby in Dickens's Bleak House neglects her family for charity abroad, a classic meddling philanthropist
an ungrammatical way of saying 'do better'

explanation.surface: A judgement on a Dickens character who ought to mend her ways, voiced in sloppy grammar.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Jellyby is the 'telescopic philanthropist' of Dickens's Bleak House, devoted to an African mission while her own children go hungry.
explanation.definitionFit: A do-gooder is a well-meaning but often interfering reformer, exactly what Dickens satirises in Mrs Jellyby.

clue.text: Fast direction out of city

indicators.note: out of says a compass direction is taken away from the city

parts.note: Preston is a city in Lancashire, northern England
N is north, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Instructions for the quickest route out of town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes N from PRESTON.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical tempo marking telling players to go very quickly.

clue.text: Made a sharp noise, talking in a trance

indicators.note: talking says the word for making a sharp noise is to be heard, not read

parts.note: rapped means knocked sharply, made a sharp noise

explanation.surface: Someone knocked sharply while chatting in a dreamlike state.
explanation.walkthrough: RAPPED and RAPT are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapt means completely absorbed or entranced, as when spellbound by music.

clue.text: Cut being painful, get on computer to cancel golf

parts.note: tender means sore, painful to the touch

indicators.note: to cancel says the letter for golf is struck out of the log-in phrase

parts.note: to log in is to get on to a computer
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone sore from a cut logs on to a computer to call off a round of golf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cancel' removes G from LOGIN, leaving LOIN. 'Cut' is a cut of meat, not a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderloin is a prime cut of beef or pork taken from the loin.

clue.text: Superfluous measure, so I took some back

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone took back part of an unnecessary measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks ESOITO from 'measure, so I took' and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Otiose means serving no practical purpose, so it is redundant or unnecessary.

clue.text: Confident visionary said alternative's not on at first

indicators.note: at first says the trimmed alternative comes before the visionary part
not says the word on is dropped from the word for alternative

parts.note: an option is an alternative

indicators.note: said says the word for visionary is heard, not spelt

parts.note: a mystic is a visionary, a seer

explanation.surface: A self-assured seer remarks that an alternative was initially not on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'visionary said' is a homophone of MYSTIC, spelt with an I; 'at first' puts the shortened alternative before it, though the clue gives it second.
explanation.definitionFit: An optimistic person is hopeful and confident about how things will turn out.

clue.text: Fill with enthusiasm to revolutionise green lives on Earth

indicators.note: to revolutionise says the letters of green are turned upside down into a new order

parts.note: is means exists, lives

explanation.surface: A campaigner aims to inspire people to make a green revolution on the planet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to revolutionise' rearranges GREEN into ENERG.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise someone is to fire them up and fill them with vigour.

clue.text: Club swam the Serpentine

indicators.note: serpentine means winding and twisting, so the letters wriggle into a new order

explanation.surface: A sports club swam across the Serpentine, the lake in London's Hyde Park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Serpentine' looks like the London lake but is the anagram signal on SWAMTHE. West Ham United is a London football club.
explanation.definitionFit: West Ham United is a Premier League football club from east London.

clue.text: Granted that a large idea may fall short

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: fall short says the word for idea loses its last letter

parts.note: a thought is an idea

explanation.surface: Conceding that a grand idea might not succeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may fall short' drops the final T of THOUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Although concedes a point, like 'even though' or 'admittedly' at the start of a clause.

clue.text: Tenor joins singing group during quiet day off

indicators.note: during says the group and tenor sit within the word for quiet

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: joins says the tenor comes straight after the group

parts.note: ABBA is the Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: A tenor teams up with a choir on a peaceful day of rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' puts ABBAT inside SH.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of rest from work in Jewish and Christian tradition.

clue.text: Be inactive, as old vein's opening in heart

indicators.note: in says the old letter and the vein's first letter go inside the word for heart

parts.note: ticker is slang for the heart

indicators.note: opening says only the first letter of vein is used

explanation.surface: An old vein's opening in the heart makes it sluggish, a medical picture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts OV inside TICKER. An engine that ticks over idles, running without doing any work.
explanation.definitionFit: To tick over is to idle like an engine, keeping going at a minimal level without real activity.

clue.text: Goat is ready to start getting drunk, a debauchee

indicators.note: getting drunk says the letters stagger about into a new order
to start says only the first letter of ready is taken

explanation.surface: A lecherous goat is all set to start drinking, a rake in the making.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to start' gives R from 'ready' and 'getting drunk' rearranges GOATISR.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgiast takes part in orgies, so is a dissolute pleasure-seeker or debauchee.

clue.text: Appalling racism — it can be very wounding

indicators.note: appalling means dreadful, so the letters are put into a dreadful mess

explanation.surface: A condemnation of racism and how hurtful it can be.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as moral comment on racism's harm; the wounding is done by a curved sword.
explanation.definitionFit: A scimitar is a curved Middle Eastern sabre, a blade capable of inflicting serious wounds.

clue.text: Kidnapper's instruction to make a turn in vehicle

indicators.note: in says the page-turning instruction goes inside the word for vehicle

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
PTO, please turn over, is the instruction at a page's foot

explanation.surface: A kidnapper tells the getaway driver to turn the car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a turn' suggests driving but means turning a page: PTO stands for 'please turn over'.
explanation.definitionFit: A captor is someone who holds another person prisoner, as a kidnapper does.

clue.text: Glimpse a drum kit, half missing

indicators.note: half missing says only the first half of the word for drum kit is kept

parts.note: a drum kit is percussion

explanation.surface: Catching sight of a drum set with half its pieces gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half missing' keeps PERCU, the first five of PERCUSSION's ten letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An aperçu is a brief insight or quick look at something, a glimpse.

clue.text: Ridiculous way muscles bend at the top

indicators.note: in a down clue, at the top says the muscles and bend sit above the word for way

parts.note: abs are abdominal muscles
a U is a U-bend, a bend shaped like the letter
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A silly path where muscles flex at the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'at the top' puts ABSU above RD.
explanation.definitionFit: Absurd means wildly unreasonable or laughable, hence ridiculous.

clue.text: Agent finally disowns politicians, a spooky set

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent

indicators.note: finally says only the last letter of disowns is used

parts.note: Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A secret agent finally breaks with Conservative politicians, a sinister bunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spooky' plays on spook, slang for a spy, rather than meaning eerie; the set is a collection of tales about spooks.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of thrillers about espionage is a spooky set because a spook is slang for a secret agent.

clue.text: Sellers say 'Don't stop'

definitions.meaning: Peter Sellers was one of the ..., the stars of the BBC radio comedy The ... Show

explanation.surface: A salesperson urges someone to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sellers' looks like salespeople but is Peter Sellers, one of the comic stars of The Goon Show, a 1950s BBC radio comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Goon is a member of the Goon Show cast, of whom Sellers was an example; 'go on' urges continuing.

clue.text: See 2
Drinking too much, bishop goes off dribbling

indicators.note: goes off says the bishop leaves the word for drinking too much

parts.note: boozing means drinking heavily
B is the chess notation for bishop

explanation.surface: A drunken bishop wanders off, slobbering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes off' removes B from BOOZING.
explanation.definitionFit: Oozing describes liquid seeping out slowly, much as dribbling does.

clue.text: Extremely selfish, muscular Atlas did

indicators.note: extremely says only the outermost letters of selfish are taken

parts.note: rugged means strong and muscular

explanation.surface: A description of the mythical Titan Atlas as brawny and self-centred.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition alludes to Ayn Rand's novel Atlas Shrugged.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlas Shrugged is Ayn Rand's novel title, so shrugging is what the title says Atlas did.
